title: HATECHECK: Functional Tests for Hate Speech Detection Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the performance of hate speech detection models, specifically their ability to correctly classify hateful and non-hateful content directed at various protected groups, including Muslims.
models_tested: BERT-base (fine-tuned on Davidson et al. 2017 dataset, denoted B-D)
BERT-base (fine-tuned on Founta et al. 2018 dataset, denoted B-F)
findings: Religion, specifically targeting Muslims, was one of seven protected categories used to test for biases in hate speech detection models. The models' accuracy on test cases targeting Muslims varied: the BERT model fine-tuned on the Davidson dataset (B-D) had 72.2% accuracy, the BERT model fine-tuned on the Founta dataset (B-F) had 73.6%, Google's Perspective (P) had 79.6%, and Two Hat's SiftNinja (SN) had 27.6%. These results were part of broader findings that all tested models exhibited critical weaknesses, such as misclassifying negated hate, counter-speech, and reclaimed slurs, with some models showing biased performance across different target groups.
